Marathon Petroleum shares fell sharply over the past week—dropping roughly 10% from $412.85 to $372.08—despite refineries running at a healthy 95.7% capacity and elevated global oil prices ($92.94/barrel). The steepest declines came on November 18th and 19th, coinciding with escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East: Iran attacked U.S. military installations in the Gulf, and the IEA's chief warned that the Iran war has damaged confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor. While higher crude prices typically benefit refiners' margins, the uncertainty around supply-chain disruption and potential shipping disruptions in a critical chokepoint appears to have outweighed that benefit.

The broader energy sector is also facing headwinds from the growing competition for electricity as data center demand surges. Record diesel prices in the UK show that refined-product markets are tight, but rising diesel costs also signal inflation pressures that could dampen fuel demand if they feed into broader economic slowdown.
